segments.text: Lesson 31
segments.translation: 第31课

segments.text: A lovable eccentric
segments.translation: 一个可爱的怪人

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: Why did the shop assistant refuse to serve Dickie?
segments.translation: 为什么店员拒绝接待 Dickie？

segments.text: True eccentrics never deliberately set out to draw attention to themselves.
segments.translation: 真正的怪人从不有意引人注目。

segments.text: They disregard social conventions without being conscious that they are doing anything extraordinary.
segments.translation: 他们不顾社会习俗，并未意识到自己正在做任何非凡的事情。

segments.text: This invariably wins them the love and respect of others, for they add colour to the dull routine of everyday life.
segments.translation: 这总是使他们赢得他人的爱戴和尊重，因为他们为枯燥的日常生活增添了色彩。

segments.text: Up to the time of his death, Richard Colson was one of the most notable figures in our town.
segments.translation: 直到去世前，Richard Colson 一直是我们镇上最显赫的人物之一。

segments.text: He was a shrewd and wealthy businessman,
segments.translation: 他是个精明而富有的商人，

segments.text: but most people in the town hardly knew anything about this side of his life.
segments.translation: 但镇上大多数人对他生活的这一面几乎一无所知。

segments.text: He was known to us all as Dickie and his eccentricity had become legendary long before he died.
segments.translation: 我们大家都叫他 Dickie，很久在他去世前，他的怪癖就已经成了传奇故事。

segments.text: Dickie disliked snobs intensely.
segments.translation: Dickie 极其厌恶势利小人。

segments.text: Though he owned a large car, he hardly ever used it, preferring always to go on foot.
segments.translation: 虽然他有一辆大轿车，但他几乎从不使用，总是喜欢步行。

segments.text: Even when it was raining heavily, he refused to carry an umbrella.
segments.translation: 甚至当下大雨时，他也不愿撑伞。

segments.text: One day, he walked into an expensive shop after having been caught in a particularly heavy shower.
segments.translation: 有一天，他在遭到一场特大阵雨袭击后，走进了一家高级商店。

segments.text: He wanted to buy a ￡300 watch for his wife,
segments.translation: 他想给妻子买一块价值300英镑的手表，

segments.text: but he was in such a bedraggled condition that an assistant refused to serve him.
segments.translation: 但他那是那副浑身湿透、邋里邋遢的样子，以致店员拒绝接待他。

segments.text: Dickie left the shop without a word and returned carrying a large cloth bag.
segments.translation: Dickie 一言不发地离开了商店，回来时拎着一个大布袋。

segments.text: As it was extremely heavy, he dumped it on the counter.
segments.translation: 由于布袋极重，他把它砰的一声扔在了柜台上。

segments.text: The assistant asked him to leave, but Dickie paid no attention to him and requested to see the manager.
segments.translation: 店员叫他走开，但 Dickie 没理会他，要求见经理。

segments.text: Recognizing who the customer was,
segments.translation: 经理认出了这位顾客，

segments.text: the manager was most apologetic and reprimanded the assistant severely.
segments.translation: 连声道歉，并严厉地训斥了店员一番。

segments.text: When Dickie was given the watch, he presented the assistant with the cloth bag.
segments.translation: 当 Dickie 拿到手表时，他把布袋交给了店员。

segments.text: It contained ￡300 in pennies.
segments.translation: 袋里装的是300英镑，全是便士。

segments.text: He insisted on the assistant's counting the money before he left--30, 000 pennies in all!
segments.translation: 他坚持要店员在他离开之前点清这笔钱——总共3万便士！

segments.text: On another occasion, he invited a number of important critics to see his private collection of modern paintings.
segments.translation: 还有一次，他邀请了许多重要的评论家，去参观他私人收藏的现代绘画。

segments.text: This exhibition received a great deal of attention in the press,
segments.translation: 这次展览引起了报界的极大关注，

segments.text: for though the pictures were supposed to be the work of famous artists,
segments.translation: 因为尽管这些画理应是名家的作品，

segments.text: they had in fact been painted by Dickie.
segments.translation: 但实际上都是 Dickie 自己画的。

segments.text: It took him four years to stage this elaborate joke simply to prove that critics do not always know what they are talking about.
segments.translation: 他费了4年时间来策划这个精心设计的玩笑，仅仅是为了证明评论家们并不总是知道他们在说些什么。
